La tercera curva de ese ejemplo tiene un: The third curve in that example has an odd name in English, the witch of Agnesi, and it comes from a translation error. Maria Gaetana Agnesi, in Milan, published in 1748 the Instituzioni analitiche, one of the first complete textbooks of differential and integral calculus, written for teaching. She called the curve versiera, “the one that turns”, and an English translator confused it with avversiera, “witch”. The book was so good that the Academy of Bologna appointed her a professor; she ended up leaving mathematics to devote herself to caring for the poor and the sick of her city.
